summary: Dedicated pool throughput collapse during multi-region peak — hidden stream crosstalk and rapid GPU-credit drain
description:
Issue summary:
Customer DataWarden reported sharp drop in dedicated-pool throughput beginning 2026-03-12 09:16 UTC with elevated p95/p99 and request queueing. Impact: multi-tenant dedicated pool in us-east experienced sustained throughput degradation for ~2 hours and intermittent 5xx for the customer's high-priority routes.

Impact:
- DataWarden reported 40% reduction in sustained throughput and repeated request timeouts for batched endpoints.
- End-user application errors and retries increased client-side latency by ~600ms on average.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id dp-8475 (us-east primary, eu-west failover).
- Customer tier: dedicated (reserved capacity).
- Models: gpt-large-1 for primary route; open-8b-quant used for experimental fallbacks.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Run steady batched traffic (payload ~120 tokens) to endpoint /v1/generate at 200 concurrent connections.
2) Observe queue growth and p99 spikes starting after ~15 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler did not trigger a pool expansion despite rising queue length; allocations briefly spiked then silently failed to attach to GPUs.
- Telemetry shows short-lived but frequent GPU-credit exhaustion events for several nodes (credit counter dropped to zero) followed by slow replenishment.
- Long-lived low-CPU streams (keepalives with heavy KV cache) owned persistent slots and serialized batch scheduling.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler expands/reschedules capacity before sustained queue increases and avoids repeated credit exhaustion.

Immediate logs/links:
- Perf dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/pool/dp-8475?from=2026-03-12T08:45Z&to=2026-03-12T12:00Z
- Allocator logs (sample): "ERROR attach: gpu-credit=0; attach_retries=3; reason=io_wait"
- Customer-provided trace: trace_id=dw-20260312-09-18
comments: 2026-03-12 09:40 - Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged. Collected traces and requested pool-id and recent job ids from customer. Escalated to infra on-call.

2026-03-12 10:05 - SRE (Marco Liu): Observed frequent gpu-credit underflow on 4 nodes in pool dp-8475. Created temporary routing delta to move non-critical fallbacks to eu-west to reduce pressure. Noted allocator attach_retries surge.

2026-03-12 11:00 - Engineering (Priya Nair): Hypothesis: long-lived streams with KV-cache pinning are preventing fair batch packing causing slot serialization; combined with a burst of small short-lived streams causing credit drain on NVLINK-bound nodes. Asked for core dumps from affected node 10.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 11:20 - Collected node-level telemetry: GPU temperature normal, but PCIe/rx stalls correlate with credit exhaustion windows.
Queueing pattern: interleaved long-tail connections (keepalive) occupying batch slots, preventing coalescing of new requests into high-utilization batches.
Autoscaler logs: scale_decision ignored due to transient attach failures; autoscaler backoff timer increased because attach_retries > threshold.
Customer traffic pattern: simultaneous multi-region failover traffic for 09:00 UTC marketing event amplified load on reserved pool.
root_cause: Combination of slot serialization from long-lived KV-cache streams and rapid GPU-credit depletion on a subset of NVLINK-backed hosts. The autoscaler backoff logic suppressed expansion because attach retries to those nodes repeatedly failed, so the scheduler reduced active scaling attempts leading to prolonged queue growth.
workaround:
1) Rerouted non-critical fallback traffic to eu-west pool to reduce immediate pressure.
2) Manually drained two affected nodes (node-10, node-12) and forced reattach after clearing stale keepalive leases.
3) Temporarily increased autoscaler aggressive_retry window to allow additional attach attempts during recovery.
resolution: Partial: Throughput recovered to ~95% baseline after draining problematic nodes and routing shift at 2026-03-12 11:50 UTC. Root-cause mitigation plan in progress (see follow-up). Full closure pending implementation of scheduler fairness and gpu-credit guardrails.
timeline_summary: 2026-03-12 09:16 - Incident begins; 09:40 - Support acknowledged and escalated; 10:05 - SRE observes gpu-credit underflow; 11:00 - Eng hypothesis established; 11:50 - mitigation routing + node drains restored capacity; ongoing follow-up assigned.
follow_up_actions: Create a scheduler patch to prioritize eviction of stale keepalive-owned slots after X minutes of low-CPU occupancy (owner: serving-runtime, ETA 2 weeks)
Add gpu-credit sentinel metric to autoscaler decision path so nodes with recent underflow are deprioritized for new attaches (owner: allocator, ETA 1 week)
Run dedicated-pool chaos test (simulate many long-lived streams + bursty short streams) in staging to validate fixes (owner: SRE, ETA 3 days)
Notify DataWarden with post-incident summary and recommended client-side keepalive tuning (Support: send by 2026-03-16)
